Playbook.name: Kaspersky — Behavioral Threat Blocked (Adaptive Anomaly Control) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: Kaspersky's behavioral/adaptive-anomaly control blocked suspicious behavior (GNRL_EV_ADSEC_DETECT) - e.g. an unusual process action matching an attack pattern. Triage: real malicious behavior, or a legitimate-but-unusual application action?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Behavioral detections catch fileless/novel threats that signatures miss.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Kaspersky Security Center CEF (verified live). Fields: destination.domain (the affected ENDPOINT, not the collector), destination.user.name, cef.device.event_class_id, cef.name, message (malware name/path/SHA256), source.ip. Use destination.domain as the host of interest.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the Kaspersky event is an active threat requiring response or a contained/benign detection.

Step.name: Confirm the Kaspersky detection and the affected endpoint
Step.Purpose: Identify the endpoint (destination.domain), the threat name and the result (cured/blocked/not-cured).
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE cef.device.vendor == "KasperskyLab" AND (cef.device.event_class_id == "GNRL_EV_ADSEC_DETECT") AND destination.domain == "$endpoint" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, cef.device.event_class_id, cef.name, destination.domain, destination.user.name, message | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: Read the message for the blocked behavior and process. A script interpreter spawning from Office, or an injection pattern, is malicious; an unusual but legitimate LOB-app action is benign.

Step.name: Other Kaspersky events on this endpoint (scope)
Step.Purpose: Multiple detections or a management-drop on the same endpoint indicate active compromise vs a single caught object.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE cef.device.vendor == "KasperskyLab" AND destination.domain == "$endpoint" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), classes = VALUES(cef.device.event_class_id), threats = VALUES(cef.name) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Several distinct threats/classes on one endpoint in the window = active compromise; a single blocked object = contained.

Node.Condition: A blocked attack-pattern behavior (injection, LOLBin, script-from-Office) on the endpoint.
Kaspersky cured/blocked the object and no further activity on the endpoint.
A business app repeatedly tripping the anomaly control.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-KAS-DETECT, INV-02-KAS-SCOPE to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: A legitimate application performing an unusual-but-benign action.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the object was neutralised; close as benign_activity.

TruePositive.Definition: Real malicious behavior blocked by behavior analysis.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate the endpoint; full scan; capture sample; open IR.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An over-aggressive anomaly rule flagging a business app.

Indicators.Item: A business app repeatedly tripping the anomaly control.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Identify the affected endpoint (destination.domain) and the threat.
If malware active/uncured or spreading, isolate the endpoint.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the endpoint; run a full scan; capture the sample; open IR.
Hunt the same malware/hash across endpoints.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Ensure Kaspersky is enforcing + updated; add the hash/IOC to blocklists; verify EDR coverage.

QualityChecks.Check: Kaspersky reports the endpoint in destination.domain (host.* is the collector pod) - always pivot on destination.domain.
The CEF pipeline occasionally mislabels events - see the pipeline health note in the phase-1 report.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Endpoint isolated + cleaned; hash hunted; no spread.
